g.text: The clean up is done in place on the main loop thread, not on a worker.
Known limitation: if the component crashes right after reaching its
ready condition, its recovery or activation task may still be finishing
on a worker while the main loop deactivates it.
true if a restart recovery action is configured
The subsequent transition will restart it if required for the new Run Target.
The transition or recovery fails: cancel() moves the Graph to kAborting
(or kUndefinedState if no jobs are running) and stops the ongoing jobs.
task is taken by a free worker
Restarts the process with the same number of start
A cancelled recovery is never reported as a recovery failure.
Otherwise the Graph stays in kComponentRecovery.
The active Run Target did not change, so no activation is reported.
cancel(): kAborting while other jobs are running, kUndefinedState
after the last one. The main loop then starts the pending Run Target,
or the fallback Run Target otherwise.
Only happens in kAborting. kUndefinedState after the last job.
A Run Target request for a different Run Target, or a shutdown, while in kComponentRecovery
cancels the ongoing recoveries: the Graph moves to kAborting and stops their stop token.
